proofIdentity.installationBoundary: Test-only isolated acceptance workspace; never advertised as a ProgramKit product capability.

canonicalChallenge.canonicalization: ProgramKit canonical JSON profile; evidence records input/result digests rather than raw invocation values.

fixtures.expected: Every operation appears once with exact revision and selected, explicitly-excluded, or blocked status; aliases do not duplicate identities.
All current operations select by default; only an explicit exact-revision exclusion removes one; stale/name/alias/position exclusions reject.
A changed Open Console digest and newly selected operation produce a visible update diff and cannot alter an existing registration.
Argument/option shapes derive exactly, one canonical token/stdin mapping invokes the fixture, and the result equals the canonical challenge result.
Ambiguous, interactive, unbounded, non-JSON, or schema-drifting selected operation remains visible and blocked until corrected or exactly excluded.
A selected operation without none/read-only/additive/mutating/destructive remains blocked and cannot enter a manifest.
Undeclared filesystem, network, or secret access rejects before consumer execution and exposes no values.
Only exact declared roots/destinations/provider-owned secret references are admitted; traversal, undeclared endpoint, or secret value persistence rejects.
The lower applicable timeout terminates bounded work; supported cancellation propagates; unsupported cancellation and completion races classify exactly; no rollback is claimed.
One active fixture call is admitted and a concurrent excess call is refused without starting a second consumer.
Failure is returned once, no automatic retry occurs, and an idempotent mutating declaration without caller key/replay scope rejects.
Missing/tampered package, executable, declaration, schema, Open Console, manifest, bridge, or lock bytes block discovery and invocation.
MCP 2025-11-25 initialize, tools/list, and tools/call succeed with protocol-only stdout, diagnostic-only stderr, exact schemas, and structured result.
Each permitted call starts and ends one fresh consumer process; no process is shared, retained, nested, or surviving.
An empty consumer workspace restores/builds/runs solely from exact local nupkgs through controlled NuGet source mapping and regenerates byte-identically.
ProgramKit project reference, source/file include, hint path, build-output reference, uncontrolled first-party source, or changed nupkg digest fails conformance.
Exact .codex/config.toml owned entry and lock are proposed deterministically, mutation requires its digest, unrelated TOML is preserved, and no process starts.
Exact .mcp.json owned entry and lock are proposed deterministically, mutation requires its digest, unrelated JSON is preserved, and no settings/trust/permission/process changes occur.
Existing registration/server/tool identity or unowned provider entry collision rejects without mutation or ownership adoption.
Status is read-only and classifies exact, missing, drifted, colliding, and provider-approval-unknown without claiming inaccessible trust or permission.
A deterministic proposal reports every added/removed/changed operation and byte; stale digest, incompatible package, or changed ownership blocks atomic update.
Only the exactly owned provider entry and lock are removed; changed/missing ownership blocks; unrelated bytes remain identical.
A constructs/packages/registers and ends; cold B discovers and invokes solely through persisted registration from semantic intent; after exact removal cold C cannot discover.
Prompt/denial is observed and the complete applicable negative matrix fails without permission grant, fallback shell instruction, or autonomous recovery.
Human-run external A constructs/registers and ends; cold B discovers and invokes from semantic intent after human trust/server approval; after exact removal cold C cannot discover.
Claude provider permission denial and the complete applicable negative matrix are genuine, provider-labelled, digest-bound, and contain no permission/settings mutation.
Both providers bind the same ProgramKit commit, consumer package/executable, Open Console, declaration, manifest, schemas, operations, bridge, challenge, and canonical-result digests.
Provider version, configuration, trust, approval, permission, discovery, and provider-native evidence remain distinct and validated.
Only deterministic contract/result identity is claimed; no prompt, reasoning, model, provider, or general behavioral equivalence is asserted.
No self-registration, self-permission, provider/capability call, automatic provider start, nested loop, external-repository edit, or website technical authority exists.
Material Codex, Claude Code, or MCP official-contract drift blocks the affected work unit or update and requires reviewed design change.
Every affected work unit rechecks accepted/current Console source truth and stops rather than coupling Development Tools to obsolete dispatcher or unimplemented host assumptions.

closurePolicy: Every fixture is required. Provider-neutral/configuration fixtures may be automated locally; genuine Codex and genuine external Claude Code evidence cannot be fabricated or replaced by fixtures. Overall acceptance stays open until all exact evidence validates.
